messages:
mira: Hey team — customer (joe@shopplus) reporting repeated partial SSE responses and then charged twice for the same streaming session. They say the client saw a final "[DONE]" chunk, then a new stream started immediately and billed as another session. Can we triage?

sam_oncall: tagged. any request ids or sample session ids?

mira: They attached a short pcap and a server trace. session_id in headers: s-9f3b2c. client reports EventSource + fallback to xhr-streaming. Minimal repro steps included.

joe_customer: FYI — reproduction steps i shared: connect via EventSource, stream product descriptions, after ~12s the stream truncates mid-token (last line: "...recommen") then a new connection opens immediately and our billing shows two stream-start events. No errors from our client.

ingrid_devex: can you paste the server trace lines around the disconnect? curious if we see a 499 or upstream reset.

mira: snippet from redwood-runtime tail: ```
2026-03-12T14:10:05.432Z INFO stream.start session=s-9f3b2c client=shopplus-region-1 route=/v1/streams model=gpt-open-fp16
2026-03-12T14:10:17.891Z WARN conn.write.partial session=s-9f3b2c bytes=1024 reason=client-reset
2026-03-12T14:10:17.892Z INFO stream.close session=s-9f3b2c reason=client_disconnected
2026-03-12T14:10:17.895Z INFO stream.start session=s-3a7d9b client=shopplus-region-1 route=/v1/streams model=gpt-open-fp16 parent-session=s-9f3b2c
```

sam_oncall: interesting — runtime logs a client_reset right before close, but then the platform restarts a stream immediately and tags parent-session. that should not create a billable new session if it's an automatic resume, but billing pipeline may treat it as a new charge.

ben_prodops: logging + billing handshake: we rely on stream-start event + session id to decide billing. if parent-session is set we do a credit flow, but looks like parent-session is present in the log — why was billing triggered? need to check the metrics produced by the router and the billing ingestion window.

packetbot: pcap summary (uploaded as pcap_shopplus_20260312.pcap): observed server FIN from edge-proxy at 14:10:17.890 followed by immediate new TCP 3-way and TLS handshake resumed at 14:10:17.894. No HTTP status; server responded with chunked SSE payload that ends abruptly.

ingrid_devex: two hypotheses: 1) edge-proxy early FIN due to upstream keepalive timeout under heavy concurrency; client immediately reconnects which produces a new session id, and billing ingestion doesn't see parent-session link in time. 2) TLS session resumption mismatch (client used different connection) and runtime treats it as new session for billing.

mira: customer says they are on mobile browsers behind flaky cellular networks — they don't expect duplicates but they do expect our resume logic to be non-billable.

sam_oncall: actionable plan: (A) reproduce with a local EventSource that force-closes socket after N bytes; (B) capture runtime + router spans to confirm parent-session header propagation to billing; (C) add a 200ms debounce window in billing ingestion to accept parent-session bind.

ingrid_devex: i can help build the repro harness. quick script:```bash
# simulate flaky close after 5s
python simulate_eventsource.py --url https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams --auth "Bearer $TOKEN" --close-after 5
```
we should run against staging with billing ingestion set to dry-run.

ben_prodops: also capture these metrics: router.stream_restarts{route="/v1/streams"}, billing.new_stream_events, billing.parent_link_missing. Add a trace tag for session and parent-session.

mira: customer provided a short billing dump: two events within 300ms: ```
{ event: 'stream_start', session: 's-9f3b2c', ts: 2026-03-12T14:10:05.432Z }
{ event: 'stream_start', session: 's-3a7d9b', ts: 2026-03-12T14:10:17.895Z }
```
no explicit parent link in billing export they gave (maybe scrubbed).

sam_oncall: ok first repro attempt done locally (staging) — saw identical behavior: runtime emits parent-session but billing ingestion created two separate records. root cause: the edge-router attaches parent-session header only to runtime logs but billing ingestion receives stream_start via a different async path (kafka) where the parent_session attribute is not always forwarded when the session closes mid-chunk.

mira: that matches packetbot too. can we short-term patch billing to dedupe by client + time window? eg: if same client+route within 500ms, treat as same session unless explicit new user action.

ben_prodops: yes we can do a heuristic dedupe in the ingestion layer as a stopgap. longer term we should propagate parent_session in the kafka payload. I'll open an infra PR.

ingrid_devex: for customer communication: propose we say — "we found a case where network-induced socket closes can cause the platform to create an immediate resume stream that may be counted as a separate session. We're rolling a fix to dedupe such restarts in billing ingestion and will follow up with timeline." Thoughts? :eyes: 

joe_customer: thanks — timeline please. it's causing visible double-charges for our users. happy to run tests in staging.

sam_oncall: ETA: patch to ingestion within 48h, and we'll share staging repro steps. non-blocking patch, low risk. I'll also add an observability dashboard card showing restart rate and ambiguous_parent links.

mira: i'll reply to customer with repro steps and ask for consent to run in their staging account. also include the pcap and server trace we used.

deploy-bot: prod deploy queued: billing-ingest/dedupe-heuristic v1.2 -> canary 2 nodes at 2026-03-14T02:00:00Z

ben_prodops: created infra ticket INF-8342 to propagate parent_session metadata through kafka topics and added unit tests for mid-chunk closes.

ingrid_devex: added the staging simulate_eventsource script to repo: https://git.redwood.dev/devex/sse-repro (uses --close-after flag and emits verbose debug).

sam_oncall: follow-ups: 1) confirm that dedupe-heuristic covers mobile reconnections under 1s, 2) ensure no chargeback for already-billed duplicates (support manual credits policy), 3) add span which includes client's IP hashed so we can dedupe cross-ingestion.

mira: thanks all. i'll post a follow-up to this thread after the canary results. joe, appreciate the pcap — saved us time.

joe_customer: appreciated. will standby and try staging tomorrow.

packetbot: note: PCAP shows occasional out-of-order TCP segments before FIN; could point to OTA network issues on mobile.

sam_oncall: closing loop: canary shows 78% reduction in duplicate charges for simulated load on staging. rolling to prod in 4h. will monitor billing.new_stream_events/dedupe_hits.

mira: thread closed for now, will reopen if customer still sees duplicates after prod roll. :handshake:
